Sibling of the #7917-class tolerance questions but needs no ruling — here the spec has already spoken. (Triage seat, session `session_019gCKd9EZfQ6MbGTnMHHJvW`.)

Container & model: `M`, `mode:subagent`, `model: opus` — small diff, but the stored-document consequence below is a judgement call, not a mechanical one.
Clause-②: no — this **narrows** the consumer to the already-declared contract; the spec side already refuses `filter`. Nothing published widens.
Serial constraints cleared: `packages/plugin-report` is free — no open PR touches it, and it is disjoint from all four other in-flight cards.

## Zone 1 — Triage's ruling (binding)

Queued as Bug: a renderer reading `report.filter` as a lenient alias for `runtimeFilter` — a key the strict spec **already rejects, with an explicit rename suggestion** — is the consumer-tolerance shape the declared=enforced doctrine retires. **Removing the alias read restores the declared contract.** Triage noted explicitly that this needs no maintainer ruling because *the spec has already spoken*.

Both sites go: the outer `report.runtimeFilter ?? report.filter` and the per-joined-block `block.runtimeFilter ?? block.filter`. `DatasetReportLike.filter` must also stop being an undocumented equal-status alias.

## ⛔ Zone 2 — the consequence triage's comment does NOT address. Read this before you delete.

The card raises it and I am making it binding: **a stored document still carrying `filter` loses its scope filter, and renders *unfiltered*.** In the card's own words, for a filtered report that is *"worse than an error"* — a report that was scoped to a subset now shows everything the server will return.

To be precise about the blast radius, because it decides how careful to be: server-side permissions still apply, so this is **not** an access-control hole — it is a report showing rows its author meant to exclude, silently.

**So: remove the alias read, but ⛔ do not let the key go quiet.** If a document arrives carrying `filter`, say so loudly — a dev-mode `console.warn` naming the key, the rename (`filter` → `runtimeFilter`), and the fact that the filter was **not** applied. That keeps the doctrine (declared = enforced; loud rejection over silent tolerance) without the silent-behaviour-change the deletion would otherwise cause. It is a small addition to the ruling, in the direction the ruling already points, and I am authorising it.

**If you find that the warning cannot be placed where a human will see it** — say, the renderer has no dev-mode channel — report that rather than shipping the silent version, and I will take it back to the decision box.

## Zone 3 — PM notes (verify)

- Reuse the spec's own wording for the rename hint if you can reach it; the spec emits `Did you mean \`filter\` -> \`runtimeFilter\`?` and matching that string means an author sees one message, not two dialects of one message.
- This card is one of a **named family** — #5116, #5120, #5067, #5068 are the same lenient-alias shape at other sites. ⛔ **Do not sweep them into this PR.** They are separate cards with separate consumers; a family dispatch here would be my call to make, not yours, and I have not made it.
- `#5047` is the docs half and is explicitly docs-only. ⛔ Nothing in `content/docs` belongs in this diff.

## Tests

Pin all three facts: `runtimeFilter` still applies (unchanged behaviour); a document carrying only `filter` does **not** get a filter applied; and that case produces the loud warning rather than silence. The third is the one that separates this from a silent regression, and it is the one most likely to be skipped.

## Gates

Derive from your diff — expect `Lint`, `Type Check`, the test shards, changeset gates, `Control Byte Scan`. Changeset required (`@object-ui/plugin-report`). Per this repo's policy the score is `minor` even for a behaviour-narrowing change — **describe the break in the changeset body** (see AGENTS.md §版本号策略); ⛔ do not score `major`, it trips the fixed-group gate.

## Deliver

Draft PR against `main`, first line `Fixes #5137`. Push the branch early. Return the JSON report **and** post it as an issue comment whose first line is `<!-- os-dev-report -->`. Read the full issue body and every comment on GitHub yourself; check the body for sanitizer truncation before relying on it.

**ACCEPT** — PM review of record (seat `repo:objectui`, session `session_01RV6yuVCxymHYE16PL9vQkE`). PR #5224.

- **PR shape** — draft, base `main`, `Fixes #5137`.
- **Scope** — from git: **3 files**, `packages/plugin-report` only (renderer, new test, changeset). The #5116/#5120/#5067/#5068 family untouched; nothing in `content/docs`. Exactly the declared surface.
- **ACCEPT path fork** — zero governed paths. Clean → queue.
- **CI** — 21 check runs, all `completed`: **19 success, 2 skipped, zero failures.**
- **Changeset** — `@object-ui/plugin-report`, no-major gate green.

## The Zone 2 instruction was honoured in the right way

I ruled: remove the alias read, but ⛔ do not let the key go quiet — a stored document carrying `filter` would otherwise render **unfiltered**, showing rows its author meant to exclude.

The resolution is better than what I specified. `DatasetReportLike.filter` **stays declared**, documented as *not authorable, never applied, and present only so the renderer can notice it* — so the type carries its own explanation rather than becoming a mystery for the next reader, and the renderer retains the ability to warn. A dev-mode warn-once (the house pattern from `resetColumnIdentityWarnings`) names the document, the key, the rename, and **the fact that no filter was applied**, once per offending report or block, silent under production.

**The boundary was stated honestly rather than glossed:** the warning reaches a developer at the devtools console, **not the end user looking at the unfiltered report**, and making the loss visible in the UI would have exceeded the ruling — so it was not attempted. That is the correct call and the right way to report it.

## The spot-check that matters most

**The card's own transcription of the spec's rename hint was wrong.** The issue body renders it with an ASCII `->`; the pinned `@objectstack/spec` 17.0.0 actually emits **U+2192**. The dev probed the spec rather than copying the card, matched the string **verbatim**, and then pinned the renderer's message against `ReportSchema.safeParse` output **so the two cannot drift**.

Had it copied the card, an author would meet two visually-similar-but-different renderings of one hint from two halves of the same platform. This is the **fifth** card today whose body was wrong in a way that would have reached the product.

## Reverse verification: two legs, each isolating one fact

This is the strongest form I have seen this session:

- **Leg A** — restore the two alias reads, keep the warning → **4 red**, exactly the "applies nothing" assertions; the `runtimeFilter` tests stayed green.
- **Leg B** — remove the two warn calls, keep the alias removal → **3 red**, exactly the loudness assertions.

A single ablation would have proven "something changed". Two legs prove *which* fact each test is actually pinning — and that the loudness half is independently load-bearing rather than incidental. Both restores verified byte-identical (`git diff HEAD` empty). The no-rebuild claim is justified rather than assumed: the root vitest config aliases every `@object-ui/*` specifier to that package's `src/`, so no `dist` sits in the resolution path.

**Declared deviation, accepted:** the suite was narrowed to `packages/plugin-report` per my instruction, and `check:published-dist` exceeded the local foreground cap and was left to CI — correctly, since the published surface is unchanged (`resetReportFilterAliasWarnings` is not re-exported from the barrel). Also worth noting the dev caught that an unbuilt dependency closure produces 17 bogus `TS2307` errors that read exactly like a real break — a trap worth knowing.

## Out-of-scope finding verified

**#5225**: a **pre-existing** test file makes **16 real TCP connections to `127.0.0.1:3000` per run** while still passing 42/42 — same class as the closed #3339 / #4106 / #4688, at a site those sweeps did not reach. Correctly left untouched: different defect class, so the bounded in-place exemption does not apply. Filed, not fixed, which is right.

Flipping out of draft and enqueueing.
